target_customer: Landlords and property managers of multifamily buildings with existing intercoms
problem: Apartment buildings use dumb intercoms and keys. Doorport sold a small retrofit device that lets residents open the door with a phone and buzz in guests, without replacing the intercom.
business_model: Hardware plus per-unit monthly software fee paid by landlords
product_category: Smart intercom and access control retrofit for multifamily housing

founders.name: Ben Taylor
founders.background_notes: Inman 2018 says he came up with the idea in 2015 after noticing the intercom in his apartment laundry room.

founders.name: Reggie Jean-Brice
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch in March 2019; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small Bluetooth relay wired into existing intercoms plus a phone app; limited software and simple hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware was simple and other access vendors targeted the same buildings; the retrofit angle was the main differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Alarm.com subsidiary PointCentral bought Doorport in May 2020 to add smart intercom capability in the multifamily market.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2019 reported landlords showed little interest in replacing intercom hardware, which led the team to switch from a full replacement to an add-on device.

branding.domain_note: Used doorport.com; domain acquisition not found.

rebrands.why: Integrated into the PointCentral platform after acquisition; exact naming not confirmed

brand_strength.rationale: Small team, generic compound name, no brand coverage found beyond product press and trademark filings.

pivots.to: Retrofit add-on device for existing intercoms
pivots.why: Landlords had little interest in replacing existing hardware (TechCrunch, March 2019)

outcome_analysis: Doorport was a three person team that started in the MetaProp accelerator, pivoted from a full intercom replacement to a cheap retrofit after landlords resisted ripping out hardware, and went through YC Winter 2019. It was acquired by Alarm.com subsidiary PointCentral in May 2020 at an undisclosed price. With small known funding and a tiny team, this looks like a strategic tuck-in; whether it was a soft landing or a good return is not public.
notes: Funding figures conflict across aggregators (CB Insights 150K, Village 650K, a secondary account of the founder saying over 1M from about 10 investors); none is verified, so no round is recorded. Inman 2018 says MetaProp was the only investor so far. Competitor search surfaced only undated aggregator and later-era pages (ButterflyMX, SmartRent, Latch), so the list is empty. Founder education and prior employers not found. Website doorport.com could not be fetched (DNS failure), treated as dead. The product was initially called Arrive per Inman. Whether Doorport was founded 2016 or 2017 is unclear; trademark first-use date is Oct 2017. Update: a MetaProp investment is recorded from The Real Deal (2018-06) with no amount or exact date. A VNC-linked article quotes Taylor saying Doorport raised over $1M from about 10 investors including YC W19 before its sale to PointCentral (May 2020), so recorded rounds are a known gap against that total; CB Insights shows only $150K over 5 rounds.
